suite: tests/e2e — the end-to-end recovery validation matrix
comment: The versioned truth for the e2e suite (tests/e2e/SCENARIOS.md documents every row).

Disks are FIXED-size VHDX files created by engine/.github/scripts/New-TestDisk.ps1 (diskpart-only: no Hyper-V module dependency - the CI-proven pattern from the bench lane). Each shard creates ONLY the disks it references, so shards are stateless and parallel.

Deletion scenarios are applied by engine/bench/scenarios/apply-scenario.ps1 (12 modes: recycle_bin, permanent_delete, unlink_native, folder_delete, quick_format, full_format, delete_partition, decay_50, decay_80, decay_100, partial_overwrite, mft_corrupt).

Ground truth is ALWAYS the seed manifest (engine/bench/seed/generate_seed.ps1, corpus v2.0.0: 23 real-magic formats, CJK names, long paths, ADS, hard links, sparse, fragmentation, nested trees, keep-control group) + the recorded deletion method - never a tool's own output.

Gate discipline (inherited from engine/.github/scenarios/benchmark-matrix.json): a gate must never test a documented engine gap as if it were a promise. Floors are cited from recorded runs; everything else is observe-only (recorded, tracked, gated only on execution-completeness: scan exit 0, session produced, inventory + metrics computed, recover exit 0/2, API exit 0/2, and the CLI-vs-API divergence check).

ReFS rows are the 'where the runner supports it' form: the runner supports ReFS (disk + format + seed all real), the product's volume scan does not - expect=unsupported_fs pins the clean-refusal contract (the prompt's every-unsupported-format-path coverage) and records the capability FINDING with run evidence.

Divergence gate: every scenario runs the CLI lane (engine/bench/ours/run-ours.ps1) and the API lane (engine/.github/scripts/api_harness.exe, the cr_ui C-ABI lifecycle); Compare-Lanes.ps1 proves both paths agree (recovered set + hash-match set + scan stats). Any divergence is a hard finding.

gate.note: recycle-bin deepcarve hash-recall 0.0006 on the 10,216-file bench corpus (run 42019994804, benchmark-matrix.json S-RECYCLE-NTFS) - the $R-name/pairing quality gap is the quality workstream's territory; the e2e row records the measured number against the same corpus.

floor 0.35 cited from run 42019994804 (current-corpus NTFS permanent-delete deepcarve hash-recall 0.428, floor = measured minus headroom; benchmark-matrix.json S-DEL-NTFS). Corpus geometry differs (6 GiB single-volume disk vs the bench lane's 5 GiB 60% volume) - a false red here is re-baselined by evidence, never by deleting the row.

native DeleteFileW is the same on-disk end state as permanent_delete (Remove-Item) - expected recall parity with S-E2E-NTFS-PERMDEL is the recorded expectation, ungated (the bench lane has no unlink_native row to cite).

bin-emptied deepcarve hash-recall 0.0739 on the bench corpus (run 42019994804, benchmark-matrix.json S-BINEMPTY-NTFS) - after Clear-RecycleBin the $I/$R metadata is itself deleted and payload recovery is carve-dependent.

quick-format recovery is a KNOWN ENGINE GAP (GAP-S6-4: name-only remnant scan, 0% vs og 51.5%; benchmark-matrix.json S-FMT-FAT32 note) - recorded ungated; the row still exercises the full format-recovery path end to end.

Format-Volume -Full zero-fills the data area - recall 0 is physics, not a defect; the row proves the product survives the zero-filled volume honestly (exit 0, empty tree) instead of fabricating results.
decay_50 measured 96.4% (PERFORMANCE-PROFILE.md, cited via benchmark-matrix.json S-DECAY-NTFS); floor 0.85 = measured minus headroom.
the NTFS decay_80 cliff is an allocation-hint sector-reuse effect, not an engine defect (GAP-S6-5) - judged against the physical-ceiling probe apply-scenario emits; recorded ungated.
100% reuse decay: maximum sector-reuse pressure; physical-ceiling judged (GAP-S6-5), recorded ungated.

the first 8 sectors of every deleted file's first extent are 0xAA-overwritten - those files CANNOT hash-match by construction (benchmark-matrix.json S-OVR-NTFS note); honesty about physics, not a gap.
MFT records zeroed + $Bitmap XORed - structured NTFS recovery is destroyed by construction; the carve-only salvage path is what this row exercises (benchmark-matrix.json S-MFT-NTFS note).

GATE = the lost partition is DISCOVERED (lost_partitions >= 1) AND recover completes exit 0/2 - the benchmark-matrix.json S-PART-DELETE contract. File recall is discovery-limited (43.0% measured, run 40073093997-smoke) and recorded ungated. Post-actions: the lost-partition APPLY probe (dry-run + real apply + partition-reappears assertion).
exFAT recycle-bin row - no recorded bench baseline; observe-only with full capture.
current-corpus exFAT delete deepcarve hash-recall 0.0 (run 42019994804, benchmark-matrix.json S-DEL-EXFAT) - the exFAT deepcarve quality gap is the quality workstream's; recorded ungated.
DeleteFileW parity row - expected parity with S-E2E-EXFAT-PERMDEL, recorded ungated.
exFAT bin-emptied row - no recorded bench baseline; observe-only.
exFAT quick-format row - the FAT-family format-recovery gap class (GAP-S6-4); recorded ungated.
zero-filled volume - recall 0 is physics; honest-survival row.
exFAT sector-reuse decay row - no recorded baseline; observe-only.
exFAT decay_80 - observe-only.
exFAT decay_100 - observe-only.
first-8-sectors 0xAA overwrite - hash-matching impossible by construction for the overwritten files.
GATE = lost partition discovered + recover completes; file recall recorded ungated (same contract as S-PART-DELETE).
FAT32 recycle-bin row - observe-only.
FAT32 deleted-entry recovery is a KNOWN ENGINE GAP (GAP-S6-1/S6-2, measured 0-0.3% recall; benchmark-matrix.json S-DEL-FAT32 note) - recorded ungated.
DeleteFileW parity row - recorded ungated.
FAT32 bin-emptied row - observe-only.
quick-format recall is a KNOWN ENGINE GAP (GAP-S6-4) - the scenario still exercises the full format-recovery path end to end (benchmark-matrix.json S-FMT-FAT32 note).
zero-filled volume - honest-survival row.
FAT32 decay row - observe-only.
FAT32 decay_80 - observe-only.
FAT32 decay_100 - observe-only.
first-8-sectors 0xAA overwrite - hash-matching impossible by construction for the overwritten files.
GATE = lost partition discovered + recover completes; the MBR variant of the partition-delete matrix (the FAT32 disk is MBR).

FINDING (runs 45826003339 refs-a/refs-b, first recorded exercise): the runner formats ReFS and seeds it fine, but the product's volume scan refuses it deterministically - 'scan failed: bad magic (0x50030001)' on every row - while engine/README.md claims ReFS first-class. The row now pins the unsupported-format path: the scan must refuse CLEANLY (exit 1, error surfaced, no session, no crash); the capability gap is the quality workstream's to close, after which the row flips back to a recovery gate.

smoke.comment: The e2e-smoke matrix: PR-triggered fast feedback (~10 min), CLI path only. Small dedicated disks (a partition-delete row owns its whole disk - the partition removal is destructive).

gate.note: smoke row: quick scan, observe-only - full-corpus floors live in the full matrix + the regression baseline.
smoke row: quick scan, observe-only.
smoke row: quick-format end-to-end path, deepcarve (the format-recovery surface), observe-only (GAP-S6-4).
smoke row: the lost-partition discovery gate (lost_partitions >= 1, recover exit 0/2) on a disposable GPT disk.

shards_comment: delete_partition is ALWAYS the last scenario on its disk (the partition removal is volume-destructive; reseed recreates the partition as defense-in-depth, but the deterministic order removes the dependency). The matrix's per-filesystem scenario order ALSO puts delete_partition last (the ALL-mode single-machine path shares the discipline), and shard selection follows the shard's declared order (run 45826003339).
